# Results — Study 916 (Withholding Drag) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Two legs per fund from
`yfinance`: the **total-return** close (`auto_adjust=True`) and the **price-only** close
(`auto_adjust=False`, split-adjusted only) with the declared per-share cash
distributions. Their daily difference is the fund's realised distribution — the income
that actually reached a US holder, already **net** of foreign withholding and of the
fund's own expenses. Headline pair: **VEA** (broad developed-ex-US) against a
monthly-rebalanced **EWJ/EWU/EWG 50/30/20** single-country blend of the same market,
one execution lag on the rebalance, one-way cost × NAV, no short leg (so no borrow).
Common window 2007-07-30 → 2026-06-30. As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month
is dropped) — data stamp as-of 2026-06-30.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| VEA + EWJ/EWU/EWG (total-return & price-only) | 2007-07-26 → 2026-06-30 | 4,762 closes | `ca173c825c7c` (quantlab `8c8542bdcf59`) |

The fingerprint is taken on the aligned close frame (4,762 sessions); the gap itself is
measured on the 4,760 daily differences that survive the two `pct_change` warmups, hence
the 2007-07-30 start quoted in every table below.

Also measured: IEFA, EFA, VXUS (broad) and BIL (cash leg). All price-only and
distribution legs are cached in the shared desk cache as `divs_<TICKER>_1d.parquet`.

### Labelled non-tape inputs (PROXY / ASSUMPTION — swept below)

| Input | Value used | Source | Where it is swept |
|---|---|---|---|
| Expense ratios | VEA 3, IEFA 7, EFA 33, VXUS 5, EWJ/EWG/EWU 50 bp | **2026** fact sheets applied to a 19-year window (a named anachronism — fees fell, so the 47 bp add-back is an upper bound) | fee-adjusted gap beside the raw gap, **plus a 35→55 bp fee-gap sweep (§6b)** |
| Blend weights | EWJ 50 / EWU 30 / EWG 20 | MSCI EAFE country shares | four-way weight sweep (§6) |
| Effective withholding rate | 12% central | JP 15% and DE 15% by treaty; UK 0% under UK **domestic** law, not a treaty rate | 5% → 25% grid (§7) |

## 1. The ruler works: differenced yield = declared cash, to under a basis point

| Fund | Differenced (bp/yr) | Declared cash (bp/yr) | Residual | Ex-dates |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| VEA | 302.3 | 302.2 | **+0.10** | 66 |
| IEFA | 291.3 | 291.7 | −0.44 | 29 |
| EFA | 269.3 | 269.2 | +0.04 | 47 |
| VXUS | 296.7 | 297.2 | −0.42 | 57 |
| EWJ | 147.6 | 147.2 | +0.38 | 50 |
| EWG | 232.7 | 232.5 | +0.16 | 42 |
| EWU | 373.5 | 372.9 | +0.60 | 56 |

The measurement itself is essentially exact. Everything that follows is limited by
*identification*, not by measurement error.

## 2. Resolution check — two near-twins with a known 26 bp fee gap

EFA (33 bp) and IEFA (7 bp) are the same issuer tracking almost the same market, so
their realised income yields should differ by roughly the fee gap.

| | Income yield | Gap (IEFA − EFA) | HAC *t* | 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2012-10-25 → 2026-06-30, n = 3,437 | EFA 300.8 / IEFA 291.3 | **−9.5 bp** | −1.05 | [−28.8, +6.5] |

The fee gap alone predicts **+26 bp**; the tape says −9.5 bp, leaving a −35 bp residual
that index composition (IEFA includes small caps, EFA does not) explains and the
estimator cannot separate. **The resolution floor of this comparison is several tens of
basis points** — comfortably larger than the withholding effect anyone is hunting.

## 3. Headline — broad fund vs single-country blend

| Fund | Window | n | Fund yield | Blend yield | Raw gap (*t*) | Fee-adjusted gap (*t*) | 95% CI (fee-adj) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **VEA** | 2007-07 → 2026-06 | 4,760 | 302.4 | 254.9 | **−47.5** (−1.07) | **−0.5** (−0.01) | [−69.3, +69.0] |
| IEFA | 2012-10 → 2026-06 | 3,436 | 291.4 | 257.8 | −33.6 (−2.77) | +9.4 (+0.78) | [−12.5, +30.6] |
| EFA | 2001-08 → 2026-06 | 6,244 | 269.3 | 222.9 | −46.4 (−4.11) | −29.4 (−2.61) | [−49.3, −10.0] |
| VXUS | 2011-02 → 2026-06 | 3,875 | 296.8 | 256.0 | −40.8 (−0.89) | +4.2 (+0.09) | [−56.3, +68.4] |

The gap has the **wrong sign** for the withholding story on all four funds: the broad
funds distribute *more* income than the single-country blend, not less. Once the 47 bp
fee difference is added back the headline gap is **−0.5 bp/yr** with HAC *t* = −0.01 and
a CI spanning ±69 bp — a clean null. The one comparison that clears |*t*| = 2
(EFA, −29 bp, *t* = −2.61) still points the wrong way and runs from 2001, when EFA paid
annually and the blend's three countries were a very different slice of EAFE.

## 4. Calendar-year fingerprint

The raw gap is negative in **17 of 18** complete years (only 2025 flips, +28 bp), ranging
from −115 bp (2013) to −15 bp (2009). That persistence is real — and it is the fee and
composition wedge, not a tax wedge: the blend charges 50 bp against VEA's 3 bp, and its
three countries yield 148 / 233 / 374 bp against VEA's 302.

## 5. Era cut (split 2017-01-01)

| Era | n | Fund | Blend | Raw gap (*t*) | Fee-adjusted (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007–2016 | 2,375 | 307.1 | 247.9 | −59.2 (−0.85) | −12.2 (−0.17) |
| 2017–2026 | 2,384 | 297.8 | 262.0 | −35.8 (−0.62) | +11.2 (+0.19) |

Insignificant in both halves, and the fee-adjusted gap **changes sign** between them.

## 6. Blend-weight sweep — the assumption dominates the answer

| Weights | Blend yield | Raw gap | Fee-adjusted | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| EAFE-ish 50/30/20 | 254.9 | −47.5 | −0.5 | −1.07 |
| Equal 1/3 each | 271.5 | −30.9 | +16.1 | −0.65 |
| Japan-heavy 70/20/10 | 226.5 | −75.9 | −28.9 | −1.82 |
| UK-heavy 30/50/20 | 298.1 | −4.3 | +42.7 | −0.09 |

Moving the country weights swings the estimate by **72 bp/yr** — more than any plausible
withholding effect. The "naive gross benchmark" is a composition dial, not a tax meter.

## 6b. Expense-ratio sweep — a named anachronism, swept

`EXPENSE_RATIO` holds **today's** (2026) fact-sheet fees but they are applied to a
19-year window, and broad-index ETF fees fell sharply over it: VEA's expense ratio was
well above 10 bp at its 2007 launch against 3 bp now, while the iShares single-country
funds barely moved. The true time-averaged fee gap is therefore **smaller** than the
47 bp the headline adds back — which means the headline fee-adjusted gap is an **upper
bound**, i.e. the assumption already runs in favour of the withholding hypothesis (which
needs a *positive* gap). Sweeping the assumed fee gap re-centres the same daily
difference; the shift is a constant, so only the mean moves.

| Assumed fee gap | Fee-adjusted gap | HAC *t* | 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 35 bp | −12.5 | −0.28 | [−81.3, +57.0] |
| 40 bp | −7.5 | −0.17 | [−76.3, +62.0] |
| 44 bp | −3.5 | −0.08 | [−72.3, +66.0] |
| **47 bp (headline assumption)** | **−0.5** | **−0.01** | [−69.3, +69.0] |
| 51 bp | +3.5 | +0.08 | [−65.3, +73.0] |
| 55 bp | +7.5 | +0.17 | [−61.3, +77.0] |

The whole grid spans **20 bp/yr** with a maximum |*t*| of **0.28**. No fee assumption
rescues either the sign or the significance, and the most generous one available still
leaves the gap at zero.

## 7. INFERENCE — implied gross yield and drag (not a measurement)

VEA's measured **net** distribution yield is 302 bp/yr. The gross yield is not on the
tape, so the drag can only be computed conditional on an assumed effective rate:

| Assumed effective withholding | Implied gross | Implied drag |
|---|--:|--:|
| 5% | 318 bp | 16 bp/yr |
| 10% | 336 bp | 34 bp/yr |
| **12% (central assumption)** | **344 bp** | **41 bp/yr** |
| 15% | 356 bp | 53 bp/yr |
| 20% | 378 bp | 76 bp/yr |
| 25% | 403 bp | 101 bp/yr |

The plausible range spans **16–101 bp/yr** — a 6× spread driven entirely by an
assumption the tape cannot pin down. Note also that a US **taxable** holder recovers
much of this via the foreign tax credit on the 1099; a holder in an IRA or 401(k) does
not. That distinction is off-tape and this study does not model it.

## 8. Is it bankable? Total-return race, excess of BIL

| One-way cost | VEA exSharpe | Blend exSharpe | Sharpe adv | Return adv | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +0.288 | +0.251 | −0.037 | −102 bp/yr | −1.05 |
| 5 bps | +0.288 | +0.250 | −0.038 | −103 bp/yr | −1.06 |
| 25 bps | +0.288 | +0.249 | −0.040 | −107 bp/yr | −1.09 |

Bootstrap excess-Sharpe CIs (2,000 draws, 21-day blocks): VEA +0.288 [−0.091, +0.702],
blend +0.250 [−0.132, +0.652] — heavily overlapping. Swapping the cheap broad wrapper
for the "gross-yield" single-country blend **costs about 1 pp/yr** in fees and
composition and buys no measurable tax back.

## 9. Synthetic control (machinery proof — never supports the stamp)

| Panel | Planted gap | Measured | HAC *t* | 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `signal_strength = 1` | 25.6 bp | **+25.4 bp** | +9.17 | [+24.5, +25.9] |
| `signal_strength = 0` (null) | 0.0 bp | **+0.1 bp** | +0.94 | [−0.1, +0.4] |

On a panel where the broad fund really does lose an extra 8 pp of its dividend to tax,
the estimator recovers the planted 25.6 bp to within 0.2 bp; on the null it reports
0.1 bp with a CI covering zero. The harness is unbiased — the real-tape null is a fact
about the *benchmark construction*, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** The study's own question is **not identified on the tape**. The
  measurement is exact (differenced yield reproduces declared cash to under 1 bp on all
  seven funds), but the gross/net split never appears: a US-domiciled single-country
  fund suffers the *same* treaty withholding as the broad fund it is supposed to
  benchmark, so the gap it produces is fees plus composition. That gap is **−47.5 bp/yr
  with the wrong sign** (HAC *t* = −1.07) and collapses to **−0.5 bp (*t* = −0.01)** once
  the 47 bp fee difference is added back, with a CI spanning ±69 bp, insignificant in
  both eras, sign-flipping across eras, swinging 72 bp across plausible country weights
  and never exceeding |*t*| = 0.28 across a 35–55 bp fee-gap sweep — and the 47 bp
  add-back is itself the *most generous* fee assumption available, since today's fees are
  lower than the sample average. No |*t*| ≥ 2 survives in the right direction. The
  41 bp/yr central drag figure
  is arithmetic on a 12% assumption, not a finding — the honest range is 16–101 bp/yr.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** There is nothing to act on. Even taking the inferred 41 bp
  drag at face value, no US-listed wrapper avoids it: the single-country "gross"
  benchmark is taxed identically and costs **~102 bp/yr more** in fees and composition
  (HAC *t* = −1.05 on the excess-of-cash return difference, unchanged across a 0–25 bp
  cost sweep). The only genuine lever — the foreign tax credit in a taxable account — is
  a tax-return mechanic, off-tape and outside this study.
- **What is real here.** The ruler. A total-return-minus-price-only difference measures
  any fund's realised distribution yield to within a basis point, and the desk can reuse
  it. What it cannot do is see a tax that was withheld before the fund ever reported.
